recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Cell Sandbox — A Visual Playground for the CKB Cell Model
recent_posts.author: zynor
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi ,
Thanks for the thoughtful review. I’ve revised the proposal based on your feedback. Here’s a summary of the changes:
Differentiation from CCC
Added a new section explicitly naming the two CCC tools ( live.ckbccc.com and app.ckbccc.com ) and clearly positioning Cell Sandbox’s niche: free-form, no-code cell design — the exploratory “blank canvas” gap. CCC is code-first and task-first; Cell Sandbox is design-first. The full revised framing is in the proposal.
“How to Verify” Section
Added the required section with a table mapping each deliverable to its verifiable proof testnet tx hashes, outpoints, screenshots, and explorer links. Each new template, the multi-input feature, and the script hash display all have specific verification steps.
Consistent Demo URL
Fixed — the canonical URL is demo (matches the README). it’s been corrected throughout.
Concrete Final Report Metrics
Replaced vague items with specific, measurable targets:
50+ testnet transactions sent through the tool
200+ unique users (Vercel Analytics)
20+ new GitHub stars
100+ template loads (anonymous tracking)
500+ x post views, 200+ tutorial views
Test suite expanded from 14 → 25+ passing tests

topics.title: CKB probably isn’t the first chain most people learn, but it might be the first one that makes them rethink what a blockchain is for

recent_posts.topic_title: CKB probably isn’t the first chain most people learn, but it might be the first one that makes them rethink what a blockchain is for
recent_posts.author: jm9k
recent_posts.content_text:
I came from Ethereum. The shift from EVM to the Cell Model was difficult because it’s conceptually completely different. I had some experience with Bitcoin Script, but it’s really quite different since it’s so limited.
When I started there were also no frameworks available, and no production ready examples of any kind. Nearly every developer that attempted to learn back then became frustrated and left. It’s much better today, but there is always much to improve on.
